tagline: Angola's sandspit port and colonial bay twin on the Benguela coast
summary: Lobito and Benguela are twin cities on Angola's central Benguela coast, about thirty kilometres apart, anchoring the Atlantic terminus of the Lobito Corridor railway that reaches into the Congolese and Zambian copperbelt. Lobito is defined by its Restinga — a long natural sandspit that curls around a sheltered natural harbour lined with beaches and hotels — while Benguela adds a historic colonial waterfront and the beaches of Baia Farta. The Benguela coast is calmer than much of the Atlantic seaboard, the Restinga harbour is well-protected, and the corridor's revival is drawing new investment and business traffic. Today the twin-city coast, the sandspit and the bay beaches are served only by road and informal craft — no organised passenger-vessel layer connects them.

transit_planning: Angola's central-coast investment centres on the Lobito Corridor railway revival and the Lobito port; passenger movement between the twin cities is road-bound. A structured marine layer adds the twin-city coastal link and the harbour and bay-beach corridors as the corridor draws new activity.

competitive_landscape: The Lobito–Benguela coast has no organised passenger-vessel operator; the twin cities are linked only by road and the beaches by informal craft. The Lobito Corridor revival is drawing new business activity, sharpening the case for a coastal passenger layer along a sheltered, twin-city coast that is wholly unserved by water.
seasonality: The Benguela coast benefits from the cool Benguela Current, giving relatively calm, temperate conditions; the dry season (May–September) is calmest and peak for leisure, while the warmer October–April season can bring occasional swell to exposed stretches. The Restinga harbour stays sheltered year-round.
regulatory_note: Angola's maritime passenger operations fall under the national maritime institute (IMPA); coastal passenger craft sit within domestic licensing, coordinated with the Lobito port authority for harbour approaches given the corridor's heavy freight traffic. Routing keeps clear of the commercial port lanes, favouring transparent, scheduled coastal operations.

precedents.what: Natural sandspit harbour with beach tourism
precedents.why_it_matters: A sheltered harbour lined with beaches and hotels — established leisure demand for an on-water circuit.
A reviving freight corridor drawing business activity whose passenger-side coastal connectivity is unbuilt.
